newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up, carloads flat from year ago.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up, carloads flat from year ago.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal freight rose in the week ended April 26 from the same week a year ago, while carloads were virtually unchanged, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

Intermodal freight, which does not include carloads, rose 7.5 percent last week to 165,879 trailers and containers from 154,310 in the year-ago week, while carloads stood at 351,972, virtually unchanged from 351,976 a year ago.
AAR said ton-miles fell 1.5 percent to 26.4 billion from 26.8 billion a year ago. The ton-mile is one ton of freight hauled one mile.

AAR said carloads of metallic ores soared 29.4 percent to 24,050 carloads in the week from 18,581 a year ago. Chemicals loadings also rose 7.1 percent to 33,419 from 31,207, while metals and related products increased 5.1 percent to 13,093 carloads from 12,458.
But AAR said floods in the upper Midwest continued to depress grain loadings, which fell 11 percent in the April 25 week to 21,908 carloads from 24,609 in the year-ago week.
AAR said scattered automobile strikes contributed to declines in motor vehicles and equipment, which fell 9.8 percent to 20,870 carloads from 23,142 last year.
Farm products other than grain fell 8.6 percent to 1,088 carloads from 1,191 in the year-ago week, while nonmetallic minerals also decreased 4.3 percent to 9,611 from 10,038.

In the first 17 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal traffic rose 6.1 percent from the same period in 1996. Ton-miles rose 2.7 percent while carloads increased 2.2 percent from the same 1996 period, it said.

AAR also said intermodal traffic on the two U.S. Canada-based railroads totaled 26,994 trailers and containers, up 20 percent from the year-ago week, while carloads totaled 59,341, up 4.3 percent from a year ago.

Combined total volume in the United States and Canada for the first 17 weeks was 6.61 million carloads, up two percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic totaled 3.13 million trailers and containers, up 6.6 percent, AAR said.
